## Key Concepts
- CV RMSE: 
- Log transformation
  - Used to solve skewed variable distribution for linear regression
  - log1p(x) if there are 0s in variable --> log(1+x)
  - y ~ log(x): +1% of x = +$\beta$/100 of Y
  - log(y) ~ x: 1-unit increase of x = +100*$\beta$% of y
  - log(y) ~ log(x): +1% of x = +$\beta$% of y
  - Taking log(y) makes looking RMSE useless (different scale) --> exp() to put y units back to same scale

- Square
  - Decide on visual basis (scatter plot)
  - Deals with non-linear relationships between predictor and predicted variables
  - Use I() in formula
  - linear (+), squared (-) --> rises, then levels off or falls (bridge)
  - linear (-), squared (+) --> falls, then rises (parabola)
  - Turning point: -${\beta}x$ / (2 * ${\beta}x^2$)

- Categorical
  - Reasons:
    - Variable is already one (zoning class, district, type, etc.)
    - A number beahves like groups
  - Create with case_when() --> manual bins or cut() --> even bins
  - One left out as baseline (based on alphabetical order, otherwise indicated)
  - Other category coefficients is the difference from baseline variable

- Interactions
  - Allows tilt in different groups of categorical variables
  - Measures how much the effects of one predictor varies when another predictor's value changes
  
- Fixed Effects
  - Categorical variable for a group of observations (usually a place: neighborhood, district, county)
  - Example: assign tracts to different planning districts based on area majority
  - Uses one location as a reference
  - Good for geographic price prediction
